Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'inspect' returns the accessibility tree of the front app (what a screen reader reads, which can differ from what is drawn) as JSON — per element: type, label, value, frame [x,y,width,height] in device points from the top-left, traits the type does not imply, enabled only when false, children. Call 'inspect' before a 'tap' on anything you have not located in this screen's tree, before answering what text a screen shows, and before reporting a control's state (a switch's value, whether a button is enabled, which tab is selected) or whether a sheet, alert or other modal is in front (the result says so) — never guess coordinates from memory of similar apps, and do not 'screenshot' for these. Go straight to 'screenshot' for color, images, and layout. Three reads: no marker and no x/y = the whole visible tree (the safe default when you do not know the exact label); marker = the first element, in tree order, whose label contains that CASE-SENSITIVE substring — a title can match before the button with the same text, so check the matched element's type; x/y = the element drawn on top at that point, as a tap would find it, with its descendants (a point between controls hits their container). If a marker misses or returns the wrong element, read the whole tree instead of guessing or screenshotting. Then tap the center of the target's frame. Hidden, off-screen, and illegibly small elements are omitted and counted; text longer than its area shows is cut (it ends with ...). Only the x/y read resolves occlusion, and only by bars and containers it can recognize: a frame from the whole-tree or marker read that overlaps a later sibling (a tab bar, a sheet) may be covered, so before tapping it read x/y at its center; a point on a sheet's blank area can still read the content behind it, so when the result reports a modal, stay inside it. A tree over the size cap loses its deepest levels first and says so — narrow with marker, or with x/y on the target itself: a point in a gap answers the container around it, which is no smaller; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the currently attached simulator, or the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

marker.description: For 'inspect': return only the first element (tree order, with its descendants) whose match_key attribute contains this case-sensitive substring — pass the label text exactly as the tree or the user wrote it, and prefer a distinctive fragment over a guess at capitalization. Omit for the whole tree (the safe default), or pass x/y instead for the element under a point.

match_key.description: For 'inspect' with 'marker': the attribute to match — label (default), value, or role (the element type, e.g. Button, Switch, TabBar — pass the exact name).

Show visual content — SVG graphics, diagrams, charts, or interactive HTML widgets — that renders inline alongside your text response.
Use for flowcharts, architecture diagrams, dashboards, forms, calculators, data tables, games, illustrations, or any visual content.
The code is auto-detected: starts with <svg = SVG mode, otherwise HTML mode.
A global sendPrompt(text) function is available — it sends a message to chat as if the user typed it.
IMPORTANT: Call read_me before your first show_widget call. Do NOT narrate or mention the read_me call to the user — call it silently, then respond as if you went straight to building the visualization.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

- pr-review-toolkit:code-reviewer: Use this agent when you need to review code for adherence to project guidelines, style guides, and best practices. This agent should be used proactively after writing or modifying code, especially before committing changes or creating pull requests. It will check for style violations, potential issues, and ensure code follows the established patterns in CLAUDE.md. Also the agent needs to know which files to focus on for the review. In most cases this will be recently completed work which is unstaged in git (can be retrieved by running git diff). However there can be cases where this is different, make sure to specify this as the agent input when calling the agent. Typical triggers include the user asking for a review of a feature they just implemented, the assistant proactively reviewing its own newly-written code before declaring a task done, and a final pre-PR check before opening a pull request. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

entries.name: mcp__mcp-atlassian__confluence_get_page
entries.description:
Get content of a specific Confluence page by its ID, or by its title and space key.

Args:
    ctx: The FastMCP context.
    page_id: Confluence page ID. If provided, 'title' and 'space_key' are ignored.
    title: The exact title of the page. Must be used with 'space_key'.
    space_key: The key of the space. Must be used with 'title'.
    include_metadata: Whether to include page metadata.
    convert_to_markdown: Convert content to markdown (true) or keep raw HTML (false).

Returns:
    JSON string representing the page content and/or metadata, or an error if not found or parameters are invalid.

page_id.description: Confluence page ID (numeric ID, can be found in the page URL). For example, in the URL 'https://example.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/TEAM/pages/123456789/Page+Title', the page ID is '123456789'. Provide this OR both 'title' and 'space_key'. If page_id is provided, title and space_key will be ignored.

title.description: The exact title of the Confluence page. Use this with 'space_key' if 'page_id' is not known.

space_key.description: The key of the Confluence space where the page resides (e.g., 'DEV', 'TEAM'). Required if using 'title'.

include_metadata.description: Whether to include page metadata such as creation date, last update, version, and labels.

convert_to_markdown.description: Whether to convert page to markdown (true) or keep it in raw HTML format (false). Raw HTML can reveal macros (like dates) not visible in markdown, but CAUTION: using HTML significantly increases token usage in AI responses.

entries.name: mcp__mcp-atlassian__confluence_search
entries.description:
Search Confluence content using simple terms or CQL.

Args:
    ctx: The FastMCP context.
    query: Search query - can be simple text or a CQL query string.
    limit: Maximum number of results (1-50).
    spaces_filter: Comma-separated list of space keys to filter by.

Returns:
    JSON string representing a list of simplified Confluence page objects.

query.description:
Search query - can be either a simple text (e.g. 'project documentation') or a CQL query string. Simple queries use 'siteSearch' by default, to mimic the WebUI search, with an automatic fallback to 'text' search if not supported. Examples of CQL:
- Basic search: 'type=page AND space=DEV'
- Personal space search: 'space="~username"' (note: personal space keys starting with ~ must be quoted)
- Search by title: 'title~"Meeting Notes"'
- Use siteSearch: 'siteSearch ~ "important concept"'
- Use text search: 'text ~ "important concept"'
- Recent content: 'created >= "2023-01-01"'
- Content with specific label: 'label=documentation'
- Recently modified content: 'lastModified > startOfMonth("-1M")'
- Content modified this year: 'creator = currentUser() AND lastModified > startOfYear()'
- Content you contributed to recently: 'contributor = currentUser() AND lastModified > startOfWeek()'
- Content watched by user: 'watcher = "user@domain.com" AND type = page'
- Exact phrase in content: 'text ~ "\"Urgent Review Required\"" AND label = "pending-approval"'
- Title wildcards: 'title ~ "Minutes*" AND (space = "HR" OR space = "Marketing")'
Note: Special identifiers need proper quoting in CQL: personal space keys (e.g., "~username"), reserved words, numeric IDs, and identifiers with special characters.

spaces_filter.description: (Optional) Comma-separated list of space keys to filter results by. Overrides the environment variable CONFLUENCE_SPACES_FILTER if provided. Use empty string to disable filtering.

entries.name: mcp__mcp-atlassian__jira_get_issue
entries.description:
Get details of a specific Jira issue including its Epic links and relationship information.

Args:
    ctx: The FastMCP context.
    issue_key: Jira issue key.
    fields: Comma-separated list of fields to return (e.g., 'summary,status,customfield_10010'), a single field as a string (e.g., 'duedate'), '*all' for all fields, or omitted for essentials.
    expand: Optional fields to expand.
    comment_limit: Maximum number of comments.
    properties: Issue properties to return.
    update_history: Whether to update issue view history.

Returns:
    JSON string representing the Jira issue object.

Raises:
    ValueError: If the Jira client is not configured or available.

fields.description: (Optional) Comma-separated list of fields to return (e.g., 'summary,status,customfield_10010'). You may also provide a single field as a string (e.g., 'duedate'). Use '*all' for all fields (including custom fields), or omit for essential fields only.

expand.description: (Optional) Fields to expand. Examples: 'renderedFields' (for rendered content), 'transitions' (for available status transitions), 'changelog' (for history)

comment_limit.description: Maximum number of comments to include (0 or null for no comments)

properties.description: (Optional) A comma-separated list of issue properties to return

update_history.description: Whether to update the issue view history for the requesting user

entries.name: mcp__mcp-atlassian__jira_search
entries.description:
Search Jira issues using JQL (Jira Query Language).

Args:
    ctx: The FastMCP context.
    jql: JQL query string.
    fields: Comma-separated fields to return.
    limit: Maximum number of results.
    start_at: Starting index for pagination.
    projects_filter: Comma-separated list of project keys to filter by.
    expand: Optional fields to expand.
    page_token: Pagination token from a previous search result (Cloud only).

Returns:

########## 14-inside-chat.md (FULL) ##########
# 14 — Inside Chat (Customer Service Chat)

## 1. Purpose and scope

Inside Chat (by Powerfront) is the customer-service live chat widget on Zimmermann storefronts.

Per HPC-039/040, the widget is a **direct PWA head tag** — not loaded via GTM. In the previous Magento implementation Tryzens hardcoded the script in the page head. The PWA is to follow the same pattern. Vicky@Zimmermann confirmed this approach as best practice (2026-07-02).

The PWA loads the Inside Chat script asynchronously, post-Didomi-consent, so it never blocks first paint. The site token (`INSIDE_CHAT_SITE_TOKEN`) is a public identifier held as an MRT environment variable and embedded in the script tag at load time.

Page visibility rules and widget configuration are owned by Zimmermann / Inside Chat / Tryzens — outside PWA scope.

## 2. PWA implementation summary

| Concern        | Detail                                                        |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Load mechanism | Direct PWA head tag — async script inject post-Didomi-consent |
| Env var        | `INSIDE_CHAT_SITE_TOKEN` (public; safe in bundle)             |
| Consent gate   | Didomi — consent category TBC (Zimmermann Privacy to confirm) |
| Scope          | All storefronts                                               |
| LCP impact     | None — async, post-consent, never on critical path            |

## 3. Open items

1. **The script tag / site token.** From Zimmermann / Inside Chat / Tryzens (the equivalent of what Tryzens hardcoded in Magento)
2. **Didomi consent category and vendor / feature ID.** Zimmermann to confirm the Didomi vendor or feature ID so the consent-gated loader can be wired. **Owner:** Zimmermann Privacy / Tell No Lies.

content.content:
########## 12-didomi.md (FULL) ##########
# 12 — Didomi (Consent Management Platform)

## 1. Purpose and scope

Didomi is the Consent Management Platform (CMP) for all seven Zimmermann storefronts. It is the gatekeeper for every third-party script that loads in the browser — marketing tags, analytics tags, heatmap and session-replay tools, the live-chat widget, the Adyen Drop-in, the Narvar EDD widget, and Google reCAPTCHA all wait on a Didomi signal before initialising.

In scope:

- First-load cookie banner and consent UI
- Persistence of consent choices across sessions and pages
- Re-prompt and preference-centre access
- Consent callbacks consumed by application code to gate downstream scripts
- Google Consent Mode v2 signal emission (`ad_storage`, `ad_user_data`, `ad_personalization`, `analytics_storage`)

Out of scope of this document:

- The downstream tags themselves — owned by Tell No Lies inside the GTM container
- Server-side consent recording or back-office reporting

## 2. Browser-side architecture

```
First page load
        │
        ▼
@didomi/react component mounted at the top of the React tree
   (which injects Didomi loader from sdk.privacy-center.org)
        │
        ▼
Didomi SDK initialises ─────► reads persisted consent (cookie + localStorage)
        │
        ├── consent already given → fires consent.changed immediately
        │           │
        │           ▼
        │     App listeners load gated scripts (GTM, Inside Chat,
        │     Narvar EDD widget, Adyen, reCAPTCHA, etc.)
        │
        └── no prior consent → Didomi renders the banner
                    │
                    ▼
                User makes a choice
                    │
                    ▼
                consent.changed event fires with the new purpose and vendor IDs
```

- The PWA uses the **`@didomi/react`** package to mount the SDK as early as possible at the top of the React tree. This is the Didomi-recommended approach for SPAs and keeps configuration tied to a single component rather than a raw script tag.
- The SDK's loader is fetched asynchronously from `sdk.privacy-center.org`. Configuration (notice copy, purposes, vendors) is pulled from the Didomi Console at runtime — the loader URL itself is environment-agnostic; the per-environment Notice ID identifies the configuration.
- The PWA registers listeners for `consent.changed` and per-vendor status changes. Each gated integration subscribes to the specific purpose or vendor ID it requires; on grant, it dynamically imports or injects its script tag.
- SSR HTML must not contain markup whose presence or content depends on consent state — consent-driven UI is hydrated on the client. This keeps the SSR cache consent-agnostic and avoids cumulative layout shift.
- No consent rules are hard-coded in the storefront. All configuration (notice copy, purposes, vendors) is owned by the Privacy team in the Didomi Console.

## 3. Credentials

- **Public credential:** the Didomi Notice ID, embedded in the `@didomi/react` component props. Safe to ship in the browser bundle.
- **No machine credential is required from the storefront** — the SDK authenticates using the Notice ID alone.
- **Per-environment Notice IDs:** separate Didomi Notices are provisioned per environment (Dev / SIT / UAT / Stage / Prod) so non-production traffic never affects production consent reporting. The PWA reads the active Notice ID from an environment variable resolved at build / runtime.

## 4. Data exchanged

| Direction | Data | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| Browser → Didomi | None at runtime — consent UI is rendered by the SDK from the Console configuration | n/a |
| Didomi → Browser | Consent state: per-purpose booleans, per-vendor booleans, IAB TCF string, regulation applied, opaque user ID | `consent.changed` event and `Didomi.getCurrentUserStatus()` |
| Browser → GTM dataLayer | Default and updated Consent Mode v2 signals | `gtag('consent', 'default' \| 'update', …)` |

The storefront does not pass PII to Didomi. The Didomi user ID is an opaque consent identifier — it is not joined to the SFCC customer profile and is never written to the customer record.

## 5. Consent and gating contract

Every PWA-direct integration that loads a third-party script subscribes to one of the buckets below. The storefront's configurable consent categories are **Performance, Analytics, and Marketing**, with **Required** always granted (REG-051). The exact Didomi purpose IDs used in production are owned by the Privacy team in the Console; the table is the application-side mapping.

| Bucket | Purpose family | Scripts gated |
|---|---|---|
| Required (strictly necessary) | Always granted, no banner consent | Didomi itself; SFCC SCAPI; Contentful Delivery API; PWA→MRT proxy reads; Adyen Drop-in — **not Didomi consent-gated**: payment is strictly necessary and the Drop-in loads at the payment step regardless of consent state. The fail-closed rule (§8) applies to analytics/marketing scripts, not payment. |
| Analytics / measurement | `analytics`, `measure_content_performance` | GTM analytics tags (GA4 and anything Tell No Lies routes to it); Crazy Egg (all storefronts — AAB-005) and Optimizely Web (US storefront only — AAB-004) — both frontend-direct scripts, not in GTM. **Consent categories are TBC — Zimmermann to confirm** |
| Marketing / advertising | `create_ads_profile`, `select_personalized_ads`, `targeted_advertising` | Meta Pixel, GTM marketing tags, Enhanced Conversions |
| Performance | `improve_products`, `personalize_content` | Narvar Promise (formerly CONVERT) EDD **(TBC)**, Google Maps address autocomplete, Inside Chat **(TBC — consent category to be confirmed with Tell No Lies)**, Omneo widget (vendor disclosure only) |
| reCAPTCHA | **EU & UK: consent-gated (TBC)** — loads only post-consent in those regions; no consent required on other storefronts at form interaction | Google reCAPTCHA site-key load on the relevant forms |

Adyen is a payment necessity and defers load until the customer reaches checkout, so it does not contribute to LCP on any other page. reCAPTCHA likewise defers until register / login form interaction — it loads with no consent requirement in most regions, and is consent-gated in EU & UK (TBC), providing no bot protection where consent is ignored/declined.

## 6. Performance and loading strategy

- The Didomi loader is fetched asynchronously and is small (Didomi-reported figures put it in the low single-digit KB range gzipped).
- Per HPC-013/014 the Didomi notice greys out all site content and prevents interaction until the consent flow completes. The underlying LCP candidate (the hero image) still renders behind the scrim, so LCP is measured normally; the page is simply non-interactive until the shopper completes the flow. The grey-out is a confirmed requirement (subject to final designs) — the notice is not deferred away.
- All downstream gated scripts are deferred behind their consent callback and dynamically imported / injected. None contribute to the LCP measurement on any page — **with one deliberate, scoped exception: Optimizely Web**. On the US storefront only (per AAB-004), Optimizely is head-loaded before render so its anti-flicker snippet can suppress content flash; this exception is allowed to take priority over the LCP budget. Crazy Egg has no such carve-out and must not block LCP.
- `<link rel="preconnect">` to `sdk.privacy-center.org` is emitted in the document head so the SDK fetch does not pay a cold DNS / TLS cost.

## 7. Multi-region behaviour

- A single Didomi Notice serves all eight storefronts; per-region purpose configuration is managed inside the Didomi Console. The Notice ID does not vary by region — Didomi auto-detects the applicable regulation from the visitor's IP.
- Per-region default consent state follows REG-054: EU storefronts opted-out; US domestic requires an explicit choice (no action = opted-out); AU, US international, HK, and ME are opted-in by default. These defaults are configured in the Didomi Console and honoured by the SDK when it loads. The fail-closed rule in §8 applies only when consent state cannot be determined (SDK load failure) and is independent of these per-region defaults.
- The marketing opt-in checkbox at registration and newsletter sign-up is **a separate UI control from the Didomi banner** and follows the regional defaults in the Functional Requirements (REG-057): pre-checked on US domestic only, unchecked everywhere else.
- The banner language follows the active storefront locale: English for AU, UK, US, HK, ME, and EU international; English, French, Italian, or Spanish for EU domestic. A storefront locale switch triggers `Didomi.setUserLanguage()` so the preference centre also renders in the new language.
- **Open (TBD):** consent behaviour on the Global-e-owned checkout iframe origin is not yet settled — how (or whether) Didomi consent state propagates to that cross-origin context remains to be confirmed.

## 8. Failure modes and graceful degradation

| Failure | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Didomi loader fails to fetch (CDN outage, network block, blocker extension) | **Fail closed.** The Didomi Web SDK does not itself default to denied if it fails to load — the storefront implements a 5-second timeout (a project decision, not a Didomi-recommended value). On timeout, the storefront acts as if no consent has been granted: GCM signals stay denied, no gated scripts load. The storefront remains functional for browsing and for SFCC checkout. |
| Didomi loader loads but `consent.changed` never fires (SDK initialisation bug, blocked storage) | Same as above — fail closed after the 5-second timeout; the error is logged to monitoring. |
| Consent is granted but a downstream script fails to load | The page does not block. The failure is logged. The customer experience continues. |
| User revokes consent mid-session | Previously-loaded gated scripts are signalled to disable where the vendor supports it (e.g. GTM `gtag('consent', 'update', …)`). For vendors with no runtime disable, scripts remain in memory but receive no further events; full cleanup happens on the next page navigation. |
| User in a region where Didomi has misclassified the regulation | The preference centre is always reachable from the footer "Cookie preferences" link; the customer can adjust manually. |

## 9. Open items requiring client confirmation

1. **Didomi purpose / vendor IDs.** Provide the Didomi purpose IDs backing the storefront's consent categories (Performance, Analytics, Marketing — REG-051). Also provide Didomi vendor IDs if applicable.
2. **Notice IDs per environment.** Zimmermann to provision the Didomi Notices per environment (Dev / SIT / UAT / Stage / Prod) and supply the Notice IDs so they can be wired into the per-environment configuration. Without these IDs the SDK cannot be exercised end-to-end against a real Didomi configuration.

########## 13-gtm.md — first 120 lines ##########
# 13 — Google Tag Manager on Addingwell (Data Layer, Consent Mode v2, Tag Orchestration)

## 1. Purpose and scope

Google Tag Manager (GTM) is the tag orchestration layer for analytics and marketing on Zimmermann storefronts. The GTM container is **hosted on Addingwell** — a Didomi-owned managed tagging server — so the browser fetches `gtm.js` from a Zimmermann first-party subdomain (`ruffles.zimmermann.com`), not `www.googletagmanager.com`. The tags deployed via GTM (GA4, Meta Pixel, and any other tags Tell No Lies configures) are therefore served through Addingwell.

> **Optimizely Web and Crazy Egg are NOT in GTM** (confirmed 2026-06-09). They load as separate **frontend-direct** tags, Didomi-consent-gated, not housed in the GTM container or served via Addingwell.

The storefront's responsibility ends at correctly emitting a comprehensive data layer and pointing the loader at the Addingwell tagging-server URL. All downstream tags are loaded, configured, and maintained inside the GTM container by Zimmermann's marketing-technology partner Tell No Lies, who also operates the Addingwell workspace.

In scope at the PWA layer:

- GTM container loader (`gtm.js`) injection from the Addingwell first-party domain, post-Didomi consent
- A native, SFCC-aligned data layer (`window.dataLayer`) populated on every relevant event
- Google Consent Mode v2 default and update signal emission, propagated from Didomi to GTM
- Enhanced Conversions data — a hashed email at order confirmation (REG-056)

Out of scope of this document (owned by Tell No Lies):

- All tag configuration inside GTM (which tags fire, with what data, on which triggers)
- Downstream vendor scripts loaded via GTM: GA4, Meta Pixel, etc.
- Tag-side consent gating beyond what Consent Mode v2 conveys
- Experiment definitions in Optimizely; heatmap configuration in Crazy Egg (and the loading of those two scripts, which are frontend-direct tags owned by Tell No Lies — not GTM tags, per the note in §1)

The handover boundary is fixed by AAB-001 and AAB-002: Accenture emits the data layer; Tell No Lies consumes it inside GTM.

### Responsibilities boundary — Didomi, PWA, Addingwell, GTM, Tell No Lies

| Party | Role | PWA relationship |
|---|---|---|
| **Didomi** (CMP) | Shows the cookie banner, captures consent, and signals which purposes/vendors are allowed. | PWA integrates the `@didomi/react` SDK and gates scripts on its signals. |
| **PWA** (storefront) | (1) Always emits the first-party data layer; (2) after Didomi grants consent, loads the GTM container from the Addingwell URL; (3) emits Consent Mode v2 signals derived from Didomi's state. | This is the full PWA scope. |
| **Addingwell** (Didomi-owned) | First-party hosting for the GTM container — serves `gtm.js` from a Zimmermann subdomain instead of `googletagmanager.com`. | PWA points the loader at the Addingwell URL; nothing more. |
| **GTM container** | Holds and fires GA4, Meta, and other TNL-configured tags. (Optimizely Web and Crazy Egg are NOT in GTM — they are frontend-direct tags; see §1 note.) | Out of PWA scope. |
| **Tell No Lies** | Zimmermann's marketing-technology partner; configures the GTM container and operates the Addingwell workspace. | Owns everything downstream of the data layer. |

In one line: Didomi = consent; PWA = data layer + Consent Mode + load-GTM-post-consent; Addingwell = first-party hosting for GTM; GTM = the tag container; Tell No Lies = configures it all.

## 2. Vendor relationship

- **Vendor (orchestration layer):** Google — Google Tag Manager.
- **Vendor (hosting):** Addingwell, a Didomi-owned managed server-side GTM platform. The GTM container is hosted on Addingwell; the browser loads it from a Zimmermann first-party subdomain. Container IDs and Addingwell tagging-server URLs are provided to the PWA team by Tell No Lies.
- **Container ID (likely single).** Tell No Lies expects a **single GTM container ID** across all environments (to be confirmed — 2026-06-09 call). Any environment separation would be handled via the data layer rather than separate container IDs.

## 3. Browser-side architecture

```
Page load
        │
        ▼
Didomi loads first (strictly necessary) and emits Consent Mode v2 defaults to gtag
        gtag('consent', 'default', { ad_storage: 'denied', analytics_storage: 'denied', … })
        │
        ▼
Data layer is populated with first-party SFCC events regardless of consent (AAB-003)
        window.dataLayer.push({ event: 'page_view', page: { … } })
        │
        ▼
Didomi resolves the user's consent choice
        gtag('consent', 'update', { ad_storage: 'granted', analytics_storage: 'granted', … })
        │
        ▼
GTM container loads from the Addingwell first-party subdomain
(`https://ruffles.zimmermann.com/9i683nqysc4y77v.js?awl=M8PJ5D`), when analytics or
marketing consent is granted
        │
        ▼
Tell No Lies-configured tags fire per consent state — GA4 collects (with consent),
marketing tags only on grant. All tag requests route through Addingwell.
```

- The data layer is always populated (AAB-003). It is first-party SFCC state — not a third-party script — and never gates on consent.
- The GTM container script is served from the Addingwell first-party subdomain and is loaded only after Didomi grants the relevant purpose. Because the request is first-party, it survives most cookie/tracking-prevention browser modes.
- Consent Mode v2 defaults are emitted as soon as Didomi reports user state, even before the GTM container loads. This follows Google's recommended pattern and enables Google's cookieless modelling downstream (configured by Tell No Lies).

## 4. Authentication and credentials

- GTM container ID: **`GTM-M8PJ5D`** — confirmed by Zimmermann 2026-06-10. Public; embedded in the loader.
- Addingwell tagging-server URL (`GTM_SERVER_URL`) — public, embedded in the loader. The first-party subdomain is **`ruffles.zimmermann.com`** (confirmed 2026-06-09). It is a Zimmermann-owned subdomain resolving to Addingwell infrastructure (DNS CNAME owned by Zimmermann; TLS cert managed by Addingwell). Per-environment host provisioning is a Zimmermann/Tell No Lies/Addingwell task.
- No secret credentials at the storefront layer. The Addingwell workspace API credentials live inside Tell No Lies' Addingwell account, not the PWA bundle.

### Loader snippets (Tell No Lies, 2026-07-01)

Confirmed Addingwell loader snippets provided by Tell No Lies on 2026-07-01. These supersede the vanilla GTM snippet Zimmermann sent on 2026-06-10. The Addingwell loader uses a custom path (`/9i683nqysc4y77v.js`) and `awl=` query parameter (the container ID with the `GTM-` prefix stripped), not the standard GTM CDN URL.

In `<head>` as high as possible, post-Didomi-consent:
```html
<!-- Google Tag Manager -->
<script>(function(w,d,s,l,i){w[l]=w[l]||[];w[l].push({'gtm.start':
new Date().getTime(),event:'gtm.js'});var f=d.getElementsByTagName(s)[0],
j=d.createElement(s),dl=l!='dataLayer'?'&l='+l:'';j.async=true;j.src=
'https://ruffles.zimmermann.com/9i683nqysc4y77v.js?awl='+i.replace(/^GTM-/, '')+dl;f.parentNode.insertBefore(j,f);
})(window,document,'script','dataLayer','GTM-M8PJ5D');</script>
<!-- End Google Tag Manager -->
```

Immediately after `<body>` (noscript fallback):
```html
<!-- Google Tag Manager (noscript) -->
<noscript><iframe src="https://ruffles.zimmermann.com/ns.html?id=GTM-M8PJ5D"
height="0" width="0" style="display:none;visibility:hidden"></iframe></noscript>
<!-- End Google Tag Manager (noscript) -->
```

> **Note:** The noscript fallback renders when JavaScript is disabled. Because Didomi also requires JS, when this iframe fires the consent signal is irrelevant; the noscript path is a graceful degradation row.

## 5. Data layer schema

Per AAB-002, the data layer is the single source of truth. The storefront emits structured events for the lifecycle moments below. Event names follow GA4 e-commerce conventions for compatibility with the most common downstream consumer.

> **Unconfirmed — pending Tell No Lies sign-off (open item 3).** The schema below is a proposal based on GA4 conventions and PRD requirements (AAB-002, AAB-004, AAB-005). Tell No Lies must confirm it satisfies the GTM tags before implementation.

| Event | When | Key fields |
|---|---|---|
| `page_view` | Every page load and SPA route change | page type, storefront, locale, customer hash (if logged in), authenticated state, customer group |
| `view_item_list` | PLP or search results page | list ID, list name, items[] |
| `view_item` | PDP load | item (id, name, brand, category, price, currency, variant, size) |
| `select_item` | PLP tile click | list context, item |
| `add_to_cart` | Add-to-bag success | item, currency, value |
| `remove_from_cart` | Cart remove | item, currency, value |

=== analytics.md FULL ===
# PRD – Analytics & A/B Testing

*Source of truth: Zimmermann Functional Requirements.xlsx, sheet "Analytics & AB Testing". Last updated: 2026-06-11. Signed off 2026-05-11 by Vicky Routley + Emma, Rebecca.*

---

## 1. Tag Management & Data Layer (AAB-001, AAB-002)

- **GTM container** must load on every page across all regional storefronts (AAB-001). The container snippet loads via the **Addingwell MRT integration** (per Third_Party_Integrations "Google Tag Manager" row). All tag firing rules and GTM *container logic* are owned by Zimmermann/Tell No Lies inside GTM — Accenture's responsibility ends at loading the snippet and correctly emitting the data layer from SFCC.
- **Mechanism note:** AAB-001's signed-off Zimmermann comment ("we will manage everything in the GTM container, not in Addingwell") refers to where *container/tag logic* lives — it does **not** mean Addingwell is absent from the stack. Addingwell operates as a **server-side container** routing analytics events (Third_Party_Integrations "Adding Well" row), and is the MRT integration through which the GTM snippet itself loads. Addingwell container configuration and tag routing remain out of SFCC scope (owned by Zimmermann/Tell No Lies).
- **Data layer** must be native to SFCC and serve as the single source of truth for all downstream analytics and marketing tags. It must cover, but is not limited to (AAB-002):
  - Standard ecommerce events across the full shopping journey: product viewed, product impressions, add to cart, cart viewed, checkout initiated, shipping info entered, payment info entered, order confirmed.
  - A complete product data schema per event: SKU, name, price, category, quantity, stock status, list position.
  - Local currency mapped per active regional storefront.
  - Customer identifiers to support cross-platform linking across analytics, CRM, and loyalty.
  - Attributes required for advertising platform pixel firing (Meta, Pinterest, TikTok, Google Ads, Bing Ads, LinkedIn): event type, transaction data, product data, hashed customer identifiers.
  - Customer attributes on every relevant event: hashed email (SHA-256), login state, existing customer flag, lifetime value, customer type, loyalty status, customer group, current store view.
  - Customer region on every event, sourced from both Zimmermann's geolocation logic and the Global-e platform.
- Tell No Lies owns the Data Dictionary; the GTM container consumes the data layer and routes to downstream tools. All *container/tag logic* is managed within the GTM container, not configured in Addingwell (AAB-001, amended scope 2026-05-05) — though events are routed server-side through the Addingwell container downstream (Third_Party_Integrations "Google Analytics 4" + "Adding Well" rows). Downstream, core commerce/analytics events are handled by Sparro and Addingwell (AAB-003).

> **Flag — residual tension to reconcile.** AAB-001 (Analytics sheet) frames everything as living "in the GTM container, not in addingwell", while the Third_Party_Integrations GTM, GA4 and Addingwell rows describe the GTM snippet loading *via the Addingwell MRT integration* and events routing through an *Addingwell server-side container*. These reconcile if "not in addingwell" is read as *tag/container configuration*, not the loading/routing transport — but the two sheets use Addingwell inconsistently. Confirm with Tell No Lies which Addingwell role (none / transport-only / server-side routing) is correct before build. This is a documentation flag, not a resolved position.

### 1.1 Downstream consumers (out of SFCC scope)

- **GA4** consumes commerce and customer events via the GTM data layer and the Addingwell server-side container (Third_Party_Integrations "Google Analytics 4" row). GA4 configuration and tag setup remain with Zimmermann/Tell No Lies. The PWA's only obligation is emitting the data layer (AAB-002).
- GTM container config, tag firing rules, Addingwell container configuration, and GA4 setup are all owned by Tell No Lies and are **out of SFCC scope**. **Exception (per AAB-004/AAB-005, confirmed 09-06-2026):** Optimizely and Crazy Egg are **not** in the GTM container — the PWA loads each as a **separate front-end tag in the page head** (see §3–§4). Their audience/segmentation/suppression *configuration* remains with Tell No Lies; only the script-loading is in PWA scope.

---

## 2. Consent State & Data Layer (AAB-003)

- The data layer is populated with **all** commerce and analytics events **regardless of consent state**.
- **Didomi gates at the tag layer**, not the data layer — advertising and personalisation tags only fire after the visitor has explicitly accepted.
- This does **not** contradict AGENTS.md "Do not load any third-party script until Didomi consent is granted": the data layer is first-party SFCC state, not a third-party script. GTM-housed third-party tags (Meta, GA4, etc.) remain gated by Didomi via GTM; the PWA-direct head tags (Optimizely, Crazy Egg — AAB-004/005) are gated by Didomi at injection.

---

## 3. A/B Testing — Optimizely (AAB-004)

- **Confirmed** (AAB-004): Tell No Lies confirmed on 09-06-2026 that **Optimizely is out of the GTM container** — it requires a **separate front-end tag** loaded by the PWA. This supersedes the earlier "set up entirely in GTM" assumption and the 02-06-2026 "managed by Tell No Lies" note; **Zimmermann provides the script** (TNL no longer in scope for it).
- **PWA loads the script in the page head** (AAB-004): "The PWA Kit will load the Optimizely script directly on the page head, so that it initialises before render and A/B test variants can be applied without flicker." It is **one snippet for all environments** and is deployed on the **US storefront only** (AAB-004 comment 10-06-2026).
- **Data layer** (AAB-002 + AAB-004): SFCC must still populate the data layer with the attributes Optimizely needs for audience segmentation: authenticated state, customer group, loyalty status, storefront region, new vs returning visitor, device type.
- **Consent & performance:** the snippet loads in the head before render and is **gated by Didomi consent**. Where head-loading conflicts with the LCP budget, **anti-flicker takes priority** — a slightly slower first paint is preferred over visible A/B-variant flicker (decision 2026-06-11). This is a deliberate, scoped exception to the LCP rule, limited to the US storefront where Optimizely runs. Keep the snippet minimal. Audience configuration and activation logic remain owned by Tell No Lies, not SFCC.

---

## 4. Heatmapping & Session Replay — Crazy Egg (AAB-005)

- **Confirmed** (AAB-005): Tell No Lies confirmed on 09-06-2026 that **Crazy Egg is out of the GTM container** — it requires a **separate front-end tag** loaded by the PWA. The earlier "via GTM" and 02-06-2026 "loaded directly on the frontend (provided by TNL)" wording is **struck through** in the source workbook (AAB-005, Zimmermann/TNL scope column) and is retired.
- **PWA loads the script in the page head** (AAB-005): "The PWA Kit will load the Crazy Egg script directly on the page head, to enable full session recording and heatmap capture from page load."
- **Data layer** (AAB-002 + AAB-005): SFCC must populate the data layer with page type, authenticated state, and storefront region to support Crazy Egg segmentation and suppression.
- **Consent & performance:** the script loads in the head but remains **gated by Didomi consent** and must not block LCP. Session-recording suppression and PII masking configuration remain owned outside SFCC.

---

## 5. Open Items

- **GTM container ID** — per-storefront container ID(s) to be provided by Zimmermann/Tell No Lies and surfaced as an environment variable (e.g. `GTM_CONTAINER_ID`) for the PWA loader.
- **Optimizely snippet** — single cross-environment snippet to be provided by Zimmermann (AAB-004); to be surfaced to the PWA loader and gated on the **US** storefront only.
- **Crazy Egg snippet** — front-end snippet to be provided for the PWA head loader (AAB-005); confirm consent-gating wiring with Didomi.

# Sprint Scope

*Draft (2026-06-23). To be refined as sprints are confirmed.*

Defines the dependency order of the build. Claude reads this to understand what code exists at
each stage. **When working in a sprint, do not reference code, components, hooks, or
integrations from a later sprint — they do not exist yet.**

Contentful works/integration will be done as part of each corresponding functional story.

For *what is currently done vs pending* within the active sprint, see
[projectState.md](./projectState.md). This file is the dependency map; `projectState.md`
is the live progress tracker.

---

## Current position

**Sprint 0 — Foundation (in progress).**
See [projectState.md](./projectState.md) for the live breakdown.

---

## Sprint 1 — 29 Jun – 10 Jul

**Squad A (FED):**
- Common UI Components
- Homepage & Navigation (Part 1)
- Regional Storefront (Part 1)

**Squad B (FED):**
*Not started yet* 

---

## Sprint 2 — 13 Jul – 24 Jul

**Depends on:** Sprint 1 complete

**Squad A (FED):**
- Homepage & Navigation (Part 2)
- Regional Storefront (Part 2)
- PDP (Part 1)
- PLP (Part 1)

**Squad B (FED):**
*Not started yet*

---

## Sprint 3 — 27 Jul – 7 Aug

- PDP (Part 2)

- Cart

**Squad B (FED):**
- Search & Recommendations

---

## Sprint 4 — 10 Aug – 21 Aug

**Depends on:** Sprint 3 complete

**Squad A (FED):**
- Checkout Flow & Delivery (excl. custom payments that will be done in Sprint 6)

**Squad B (FED):**
- Promotions

---

## Sprint 5 — 24 Aug – 4 Sep

**Depends on:** Sprint 4 complete

**Squad A (FED):**
- Order Management

**Squad B (FED):**

- Zimmerse

---

## Sprint 6 — 7 Sep – 11 Sep

**Depends on:** Sprint 5 complete

**Squad A (FED):**
- Payments (Adyen, etc)
- Credit Notes & Gift Cards (GiveX)

**Squad B (FED):**
- Zimmerse

---

## Sprint 7

**Depends on:** Sprint 6 complete

**Squad A (FED):**
- Returns & Refunds

**Squad B (FED):**
- SEO & Analytics (GTM, Optimizely, Crazy Egg, Inside Chat, etc)

---

## How Claude uses this file

When implementing a feature, Claude checks which sprint it belongs to and does not reference
components, hooks, or integrations from later sprints.

If a task requires something from a later sprint, Claude stops and asks:
> "This feature depends on [X] which is Sprint [N] work. Should I build a placeholder, or is
> Sprint [N] already complete?"

Reference this file in prompts when sprint context matters:
> "We are currently in Sprint 1. Build the global header skeleton. Do not wire up basket
> state — that is Sprint 3."

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

content.text: Chapter marked: "Estimate synthesis". Continue your current work.

I have comprehensive Jira + repo evidence. Writing up now.

**One consent-layer answer changes all three estimates: Didomi does not exist.** `@didomi/react` is absent from `package.json` (only 5 runtime deps: Adyen ×2, Contentful ×3). `.docs/memory/projectState.md:20` — "Didomi | Not started". `config/sit.js:46` — *"Didomi isn't built yet"*. There is also **zero** tracking plumbing: grep for `dataLayer|gtag(|googletagmanager|gtm-` across `overrides/` returns nothing.

`.docs/architecture.md`'s integration-class table is the other load-bearing evidence: **Emarsys = "Out-of-band"** (line 233), **Avalara = "SFCC (cartridge)"** (line 245) — versus Didomi/GTM/Inside Chat, all "PWA-direct".

---

## SFCC-857 — Emarsys Web Extend

Inject Emarsys' Scarab browser JS and feed it identity/browse/cart/purchase events for cart abandonment, browse abandonment and revenue reporting.

**AC quality: NO — zero ACs.** `customfield_10231` is null. The description has a heading "Outstanding Questions (**to be resolved before story can be refined**)" with 3 unanswered questions.

**What exists: nothing, and no foundation to build on.**
- No Emarsys/Scarab code. Only `overrides/app/hooks/useSubscribeSection.ts:8`, a comment about the *backend* Omneo→Emarsys path.
- `.docs/integration/` has 18 vendor docs — Didomi (12), GTM (13), Inside Chat (14), Optimizely (15), Crazy Egg (16) — **none for Emarsys**.
- No Emarsys key in `.env.sample`; every other browser-side vendor has one (`DIDOMI_API_KEY`, `GTM_CONTAINER_ID`, `INSIDE_CHAT_SITE_TOKEN`, `OPTIMIZELY_PROJECT_ID`).
- Emarsys appears nowhere in the signed-off `.docs/prd/analytics.md`. All PRD references (cart.md:124, homepage.md:90, account.md:29, checkout.md:35, regional.md:143) are the Omneo→Emarsys backend sync.
- Injection point does exist: `react-helmet` in `_app-config/index.tsx`; `_app/index.tsx:182` already uses `useLocation`. PDP/PLP/home/confirmation are already overridden → **low copy-first cost**.

| # | FED work | Days |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Scarab loader — async, SSR-safe, post-consent injection | 0.75 |
| 2 | Per-site merchant ID + Emarsys `availabilityZone` across 8 storefronts / 11 locales | 0.5 |
| 3 | Identity (`setEmail`/`setCustomerId`), incl. guest-email-at-checkout | 0.5 |
| 4 | Browse events: `view` (PDP), `category` (PLP), `searchTerm` | 0.75 |
| 5 | `cart` command on every page view (abandonment needs cart state each load) | 0.5 |
| 6 | `purchase` at order confirmation (revenue contribution) | 0.5 |
| 7 | SPA route-change `['go']` dispatch + double-fire guard | 0.5 |
| 8 | **Consent gating** — Didomi purpose subscribe, fail-closed, revoke mid-session | 0.5 |
| 9 | **Performance budget** — defer, LCP non-regression, `main.js`/`vendor.js` check | 0.25 |
| 10 | Vitest for event mapping + story/E2E | 0.75 |
| 11 | 8-storefront verification | 0.5 |
| | **Total** | **6.0** |

**Bottom-up: ~6 days** (5.5–7).

**Verdict: UNDER by ~3 days (3 → 6).** The 3-day figure prices a script drop-in; the actual bulk is the per-page-type event mapping (items 3–7 = 2.75d), all net-new because no tracking abstraction exists.

**Dependency on unbuilt work — yes, hard.** Didomi (Not started, unscheduled). If SFCC-857 must build it too, add **~5–8 days** *(my estimate: SDK mount, per-env Notice IDs, consent Context, Consent Mode v2, 5s fail-closed timeout, revoke, REG-054 regional defaults)*. `sprintScope.md` puts analytics in Sprint 7.

**Blockers:** the 3 unanswered questions; Accenture↔TNL boundary on "rules, loading logic, Data Dictionary"; no merchant ID; no Didomi purpose ID. **Duplication risk (flagged):** Web Extend's `cart`/`purchase`/`view` data overlaps the AAB-002 dataLayer heavily — building a standalone queue now likely means rework when GTM lands.

**Ask:** Tessa Turnbull / Jasmijn Tsang (the 3 questions — they gate refinement); Tell No Lies (who owns the Data Dictionary; shared event bus or separate queue?); Isabel Chaloner / Tash (Emarsys engagement status); Integration lead (Didomi funded/scheduled?).

---

## SFCC-858 — Co-browsing in Live Chat

Let client-services agents co-browse the storefront with a shopper, behind a consent prompt.

**AC quality: NO — zero ACs.** `customfield_10231` null. Description: *"This ticket is a placeholder pending technical details from Emma"*.

**What exists: Inside Chat is not embedded at all.** grep for `insidechat|inside-chat|livechat` across `overrides/ config/ worker/` → zero. The only `chat` hits are an icon (`components/icons/zimm.tsx`) and translation strings. `projectState.md:31` "Inside Chat | Not started". `.env.sample:256` `INSIDE_CHAT_SITE_TOKEN=` blank. `.docs/integration/14-inside-chat.md` exists but **never mentions co-browsing**, and both its open items are unresolved.

| # | FED work (best case) | Days |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Enable/configure co-browse in the embed | 0.25 |
| 2 | Consent prompt UI — component, copy, accept/decline, WCAG 2.2 AA | 1.0 |
| 3 | Wire consent → INSIDE co-browse session start/stop | 0.5 |
| 4 | **PII/payment masking** — card fields, GiveX card+PIN, address data hidden from agent | 1.0 |
| 5 | **Consent gating** — Didomi category, fail-closed | 0.5 |
| 6 | Per-storefront enablement rules | 0.25 |
| 7 | Tests / stories | 0.5 |
| 8 | Live cross-browser co-browse session verification | 0.5 |
| | **Total** | **4.5** |

**Bottom-up: ~4.5 days best case** — and that *excludes* embedding Inside Chat.

**Verdict: UNDER by ~1.5 days best case; realistically NOT ESTIMABLE.** The table's own note concedes it — *"Is this functionality available today? Assuming InsideChat has this functionality"*. The 3 days omits masking and consent-UI entirely. Powerfront's INSIDE does market native Co-Browse/Screen Share ([powerfront.com](https://www.powerfront.com/live-chat-and-messaging)) — but that is vendor marketing, **not** confirmation of Zimmermann's licence tier. If co-browse isn't in the contract this becomes a separate vendor integration and the figure is wrong by an order of magnitude.

**Dependency on unbuilt work — yes, twice over.** Presumes Inside Chat is live (it isn't embedded) *and* Didomi.

**Blockers:** Emma Kirwan's technical details never supplied; licence-tier capability unconfirmed; consent wording/design "TBC"; **masking vs `conventions.md`'s payment-credential rule** — an agent viewing a live checkout is a real compliance question; "Defer to future phase".

**Ask:** Emma Kirwan (the promised details; is co-browse on the contract?); Powerfront AM (native co-browse, masking controls, React SPA support); Zimmermann Privacy/legal (may agents view checkout at all?); PM (defer vs estimate now — and Inside Chat's own embed story must land first).

---

## SFCC-946 — Avalara scope expansion

Extend Avalara tax calculation to further markets (note says EU, UK, Domestic).

**AC quality: NO on SFCC-946** (null; scope is literally "to be confirmed"). **SFCC-878 is PARTIAL — 6 real ACs + 2 bracketed `[PENDING — UK and EU Domestic scope not yet confirmed]`.** The exact markets SFCC-946 covers are the ones SFCC-878 flags as unconfirmed.

**What exists — and why the FE delta is near zero:**
- `.docs/architecture.md:245` classifies Avalara as **"SFCC (cartridge)"** — no PWA-layer component by design.
- Base `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/order-summary/index.jsx:247-266` **already renders a Tax line from `basket.taxTotal`**, with a "TBD" fallback.
- `order-summary` is **not overridden**. `overrides/app/pages/cart/` holds only a drawer container + item mapper; `overrides/app/pages/checkout/` only partials — **base cart and checkout pages still render**. Tax display is entirely base and payload-driven.
- SFCC-878's ACs are all backend, and explicitly carve out FE: *"**(Tax line item display is covered in SFCC-462.)**"*
- SFCC-462 (Tech design) owns US tax display; SFCC-43 (In Refinement) owns per-market display — all its ACs are *"Given a Site Admin configures … in Business Manager"*.
- Display mode is fixed by signed-off PRD regardless of engine: PRC-05 (AU+EU inclusive), PRC-06 (US exclusive).

**The baseline is contradicted five ways** — this is the headline:

| Source | Avalara markets |
|---|---|
| `checkout.md:191` PAY-067 | US domestic, NZ, New Caledonia — "all other domestic storefronts use SFCC native tax tables" |
| `pricing-currency-globale.md:28` PRC-07 *(signed off 2026-06-24, Emma/Rebecca)* | "Avalara covers **AU, EU, US, and UK** domestic storefronts for go-live" |
| `architecture.md:245` + `projectState.md:29` *(2026-06-19)* | US domestic, NZ, New Caledonia, **EU domestic**; UK native VAT |
| SFCC-878 | AU + US Domestic (+NZ/NC/Puerto Rico landed cost); "UK and EU Domestic … not Avalara" |
| SFCC-43 | EU Domestic native; UK "to be confirmed" |

| # | FED work attributable to SFCC-946 | Days |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Regression-verify tax display on EU + UK after the engine switches (cart, checkout, order summary) | 0.5 |
| 2 | Tax label copy per market (GST/VAT/Tax) — arguably SFCC-43's | 0.25 |
| | **Total** | **0.5–0.75** |

Not FED here: tax computation (cartridge/BED); display mode (BM config); the tax line render (base, payload-driven); consent gating (N/A, no browser script); performance budget (N/A, no new script or bundle weight).

**Verdict: MIS-ATTRIBUTED — overstated ~1.25–1.5 days.** The front end reads `basket.taxTotal` from the SCAPI payload; the rendered output is identical whether Avalara or native tax tables computed it. The genuine FE tax work is already ticketed as SFCC-462 and SFCC-43 — 2 FED days here double-books it.

**Dependency on unbuilt work — yes.** Presumes a baseline Avalara integration that is "Not started", and a tax-display framework in SFCC-462/SFCC-43, both still pre-build. There is no FE foundation to expand *from*.

**Blockers:**
1. The five-way contradiction — **you cannot estimate an expansion against an undefined baseline.** Two signed-off PRDs (PRC-07 vs PAY-067) conflict; per AGENTS.md "Doc integrity" that needs adjudication, not a silent pick. If PRC-07 stands, EU+UK are already in the go-live baseline and SFCC-946 isn't chargeable scope at all.
2. SFCC-946 never names the markets; "Domestic" is ambiguous.
3. Status mismatch: table says **Approved**, Jira says **To Do** — flagging in case "Approved" was read as build-ready.
4. Adjacent real gap (not SFCC-946's): PAY-058 requires "tax and duties shown as separate line items, never combined" and base `order-summary` has **no duties line**. That IS unbudgeted FED work — but it belongs to SFCC-878's NZ/NC/Puerto Rico landed cost and PAY-059–062 DDP/DDU messaging, not an EU/UK expansion.

**Ask:** Emma/Rebecca + the PAY-067 owner (which market list is correct? — blocks the estimate); Tim/PM (if PRC-07 already covers EU+UK, is this chargeable?); BED cartridge lead (any FE-visible payload change when Avalara replaces native tables? if no, FED → 0.5d); SFCC-462/SFCC-43 owners (confirm tax-line and duties display are budgeted there).

---

## Summary

| Ticket | Table FED | Bottom-up | Verdict | Delta |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SFCC-857 Emarsys Web Extend | 3 | **6.0** | UNDER | **+3** (+5–8 more if it must build Didomi) |
| SFCC-858 Co-browsing | 3 | **4.5** best case | UNDER / not estimable | **+1.5**, or wrong by an order of magnitude |
| SFCC-946 Avalara expansion | 2 | **0.5–0.75** | MIS-ATTRIBUTED | **−1.25 to −1.5** |

Net across the three: roughly **+3 days**, but that understates the risk — two of the three rest on foundations that do not exist.

**The cross-cutting finding:** none of these three can start. Didomi gates 857 and 858 and is unbuilt and unscheduled; Inside Chat gates 858 and isn't embedded; Avalara's own baseline gates 946 and is contradicted five ways. The table prices all three as if the plumbing were already there.

**Two things I'd raise regardless of the numbers:** first, SFCC-857 will build a browser-side event pipeline that substantially duplicates the AAB-002 dataLayer — sequencing it against GTM (Sprint 7) rather than before it avoids paying twice. Second, SFCC-946's 2 FED days and SFCC-462/SFCC-43's FE tax work look like the same work counted in more than one place; worth reconciling before any of it is committed.

Two Confluence research agents (Emarsys/Didomi, and Inside Chat/Avalara incl. verification of page 385318913's table rows) were still running when I finished — the findings above rest on Jira and repo evidence, which is independent of them. I'll relay their results when they land; they may add vendor-page detail but are unlikely to move these totals.
